changes.description: change type of players.name from varchar(50) to varchar(100)
change type of players.rating from integer to bigint
add foreign key players (team_id) -> teams (id) ON DELETE SET NULL
create unique index ux_players_email on players (email)

findings.subject: players.nickname
findings.message: Dropping players.nickname permanently deletes its value in every row.
findings.recommendation: Stop reading and writing the column in the application and deploy that first, back the values up, then drop the column in a later migration (expand and contract).
findings.check_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM "players" WHERE "players"."nickname" IS NOT NULL

findings.subject: table legacy_scores
findings.message: Dropping legacy_scores permanently deletes all of its rows.
findings.recommendation: Back the data up first, for example with CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT, or stop using the table and drop it in a later release once nothing reads it.

findings.subject: check on players ("rating" >= 0)
findings.message: Rows already in players may violate CHECK ("rating" >= 0), which makes the migration fail. PostgreSQL checks every row while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock that blocks reads and writes.
findings.recommendation: Fix the violating rows first. On a large table, add the constraint with NOT VALID and run ALTER TABLE ... VALIDATE CONSTRAINT separately; validating does not block writes.

findings.subject: foreign key players (team_id) -> teams
findings.message: Adding the foreign key checks every row of players while holding SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE locks on players and teams, which block writes to both; rows without a match make the migration fail.
findings.recommendation: Add the constraint with NOT VALID, which only takes a brief lock, then run ALTER TABLE ... VALIDATE CONSTRAINT in a separate transaction; validating does not block writes.
findings.check_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM "players" AS child WHERE child."team_id" IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "teams" AS parent WHERE parent."id" = child."team_id")

findings.subject: foreign key teams (league_id) -> leagues
findings.message: Adding the foreign key checks every row of teams while holding SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE locks on teams and leagues, which block writes to both; rows without a match make the migration fail.
findings.recommendation: Add the constraint with NOT VALID, which only takes a brief lock, then run ALTER TABLE ... VALIDATE CONSTRAINT in a separate transaction; validating does not block writes.

findings.subject: index ux_players_email on players
findings.message: Building ux_players_email blocks inserts, updates and deletes on players (SHARE lock) until the whole table has been indexed.
findings.recommendation: Run with --concurrent-indexes to build it with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY outside the transaction: it takes longer but does not block writes.

findings.subject: players.rating
findings.message: Making players.rating NOT NULL fails if any row holds NULL, and PostgreSQL checks every row while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock that blocks reads and writes.
findings.recommendation: Backfill the NULLs first. On a large table, add CHECK (column IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID, validate it in a separate transaction, then SET NOT NULL: PostgreSQL 12 and later use the validated constraint and skip the scan.
findings.check_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM "players" WHERE "players"."rating" IS NULL

findings.subject: players.rating
findings.message: Changing players.rating from integer to bigint makes PostgreSQL rewrite the whole table and its indexes while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock that blocks reads and writes.
findings.recommendation: On a large table, add a new column of the new type, backfill it in batches, switch the application over and drop the old column; otherwise run the migration in a maintenance window.
